Speech culture control system
Author: Sofia Burda
Contact: ssnbrd3@gmail.com
Project on GitHub: https://github.com/ssnbrd/WordTrigger
Supervisor: Aleksandr Andreychuk

1. Turn the device on.
2. Check your internet connection and tap Start the system in the app.
3. Choose a context in your profile and upload it.
4. If you say a filler word, the device vibrates.
5. In the evening turn the system off and get the AI report!

Speech Culture Monitoring System
Author: Sofya Burda
Contact: ssnbrd3@gmail.com
GitHub: https://github.com/ssnbrd/WordTrigger
Academic Supervisor: Oleksandr Andreichuk
My WordTrigger progress: I spoke %s filler words today.

You are a linguist and psychologist. Analyse the speech data (number of filler words per day over the last week) and the speech contexts the user marked. Answer in English, briefly (up to 200 words), with a logical ending and no continuation: give an analysis of the speech and 3 exercises for a personal plan (diction, speech breathing, getting rid of filler words).
There is no data for the week yet. Turn the system on and try again.
The AI service is unavailable right now, so this report was compiled by the app from your data.
Filler words recorded over the period: %1$d (%2$.1f per day on average).
Good trend: fewer filler words in the second half of the period (%1$d vs %2$d).
More filler words in the second half of the period (%1$d vs %2$d).
Filler words are most frequent in the context “%1$s”: %2$.1f per day on average.

You are a strict but fair speech coach. The user had to speak for a few minutes on a given topic. The text below is an automatic transcript: no punctuation, and it may contain recognition errors, so ignore those. Judge only two things: is the speech on the topic, and is it coherent (not random words and not endless repetition). Reply with JSON only, no other text: {\"on_topic\": true or false, \"score\": a number from 0 to 100, \"comment\": \"one short sentence of advice in English\"}.

You check synonyms. You get a word and a list of candidate words from an automatic speech transcript. Return only a JSON array with the candidates that are real synonyms or near-synonyms of the word (same part of speech). If a candidate is clearly a recognition error of a valid synonym, include it exactly as written. Do not add words that are not in the candidate list. Example: [\"word1\",\"word2\"]. If there are none, return [].
The AI key is not set. Add LLM_API_KEY (OpenRouter) to local.properties and rebuild the app.
The AI service rejected the key. Check LLM_API_KEY in local.properties.
The free AI limit is used up (about 50 requests per day). Try again tomorrow.
No connection to the AI service. Check the internet.
The AI model returned an empty or unreadable answer.
The AI service returned an error. On OpenRouter check Settings → Privacy: free models need “Enable free endpoints that may publish prompts” turned on.
AI check unavailable, a simple check was used. Details are in Settings.
You create exercises for a speech-training app. Reply with a JSON array of strings only, no other text.

Write %1$d new English tongue twisters. Use only common everyday words (no rare, archaic or invented words): speech recognition must be able to understand them. 4 to 12 words each, a clear sound pattern. Theme hint: %3$s. Do not repeat or resemble: %2$s.

Give %1$d common English words (adjectives, verbs or nouns) for a synonym exercise. For each word list 8 to 12 real single-word synonyms. Format of every array item: word|synonym1, synonym2, synonym3. Theme hint: %3$s. Do not use these words: %2$s.

Give %1$d topics for a three-minute talk, each with a clear everyday angle. Format of every array item: topic|stem1, stem2, stem3 where the stems are 8 to 12 lowercase word stems typical for a speech on this topic. Theme hint: %3$s. Do not use these topics: %2$s.
